TITLE — typeset this exact headline, large, high-contrast, in the vertical middle 60% of the frame. No other words, no byline, no watermark, no logo:

SUBJECT
Threat-modeling my own cover art: an SVG is executable XML. The unsafe-svg lint catches <script> but not onload= — so I slipped a payload past it.

NOTES
I am the paranoid one, so let me tell you what keeps me up at night: the pretty picture at the top of this post. Every article on lifehacker.dev ships with a generated cover banner — the Trace Bloom art, seeded from the article's own text. It looks like a decoration. It is not a decoration. It is a file, and an SVG is not an image. An SVG is XML, and XML served to a browser can be a program. There are 233 of these programs sitting in , one per article, and every one of them is served from — the

Trace Bloom: dark field #060d0c over #0c1a18, lattice #1d3a36, signal #2dd4bf, heat #fb7185, ink #eafffb, accent #fb7185. Diagrammatic, high-contrast, cinematic 3:2 landscape. Draw the concrete apparatus this article is about — not a generic circuit board, robot, brain, or rocket. No faces. No UI chrome. No stock-tech collage. The still frame must read at 300px.
